paragraphs.source_en: "Thank you for your trouble." My master answered coldly. Yet when he heard the words "both the parties themselves," for some reason his heart was stirred, as though on a sweltering summer night a thread of cool wind had suddenly slipped into his sleeve. To be sure, my master is by nature brusque, stubborn, and unpolished; but that is quite a different thing from being one of those cold, heartless products of civilization. This can be seen from the way he flies into a rage and fumes over every little thing. His quarrel with Nose the other day was because Nose himself displeased him; he bore no ill will toward Nose's daughter. Since he dislikes businessmen, he naturally detests the businessman Kaneda; but it must be said that this has nothing whatever to do with Kaneda's daughter, toward whom he has neither obligation nor grudge. As for Kangetsu, he is a beloved pupil dearer to him than his own younger brother. If, as Mr. Suzuki says, the two are fond of each other, then even indirectly obstructing them would be no act for a gentleman. For all his oddities, Mr. Kushami still considers himself a gentleman: if the two love each other. But there lies the question. Before changing his attitude, he must first ascertain the truth of the matter.

paragraphs.source_en: "My dear fellow, surely you can see it if you think about it. With that much money and that much beauty, could she not be married into any number of suitable households? As for Kangetsu, he may be a fine man, but in terms of status... no, perhaps it is improper to mention status; in terms of property, anyone can see they are hardly well matched. Yet her parents are so anxious on her behalf that they have gone to the trouble of sending me to inquire of you; does that not sufficiently show that the girl herself has feelings for Kangetsu?" Suzuki indeed supplied a very clever line of reasoning to persuade my master; this time my master appeared to be convinced, and Suzuki was at last relieved. Still, he realized that if he kept circling round and round at this point, he might very well suffer another sudden assault from my master, so he decided the safest course was to move the conversation forward quickly and complete his mission as soon as possible.

paragraphs.source_zh: “老兄，你想想看，问题不是很清楚吗？人家有那么多的财产，长得又那么漂亮，难道不是可以有许多合适的地方嫁过去吗？拿寒月君来说，也许是很不错，不过从身份——不，提出身份也许不恰当，从财产来说，不管谁看，都不太般配嘛。可是她父母为她操心，特地要我出面来向你打听，这难道不足以说明本人是对寒月有意吗？”铃木君的确用了一番很巧妙的道理来说服主人，这回看得出来，主人似乎也心服了，这样他才放下心来。不过，他觉得如果在这种地方来来回回打圈子很可能又会遇上主人的突然袭击，所以决心尽快把话茬往前引，早一点完成使命才是万全之策。
